summary: Sheikh Ali Mashhour discusses the Islamic perspective on modern superstitions, specifically focusing on good luck charms and talismans as a continuation of last week's topic on bad omens (tatayyur). He explains the Islamic principle that correlation does not imply causation, and how believing in good luck charms—whether bracelets, the evil eye amulet, or various rituals—constitutes a form of minor shirk (associating partners with Allah). Sh. Ali Mashhour provides examples from Western culture, such as the Charging Bull on Wall Street and New Year's cabbage traditions, and contrasts these superstitions with the Islamic concept of tawakkal (reliance on Allah) and good thinking (husn al-dhann).
